explanation: The thumbs-up is understood in Spain much as across most of Western Europe and Latin America: approval, agreement, or 'all good.' It's used casually among friends, service staff, and even in business settings without negative connotation, unlike in Greece or parts of the Middle East where it can be read as vulgar.
local_tip: Use it freely to signal approval or that everything's fine; it's one of the safest hand gestures to use in Spain.

also_check.note: Historically read as an insulting gesture roughly equivalent to showing a middle finger, though younger Greeks increasingly use it to mean 'OK'.
In some traditional Gulf Arab contexts it can be seen as a crude or insulting gesture, so it's safer to avoid it in formal or conservative settings.
Germans commonly use the raised thumb to mean the number 'one' when counting, in addition to its approval meaning.
